beats: Divers pulled a two-thousand-year-old computer from the bottom of the sea.
Greece, 1901. It looked like a lump of rusted rock.
Then X-rays revealed over thirty precise bronze gears inside.
But nothing this complex appears again for a thousand years.
Turn its handle, and it predicted eclipses years ahead. Its maker is still unknown.
That rusty rock was a calendar of the sky. So how was this knowledge lost?
antikythera-mechanism.challenge:
🧩 Why was this knowledge lost for 1,000 years?
A) Only a few people knew it, and it died with them
B) Wars and burned libraries destroyed it
C) Something else
Answer with a letter 👇 Best answer gets pinned 📌

beats: A man hijacked a plane, jumped out with the cash, and vanished.
1971. A man in a dark suit handed a flight attendant a note: I have a bomb.
He got two hundred thousand dollars and four parachutes, then jumped into the rainy night.
But nine years later, a boy found bundles of that same cash buried in a riverbank.
The FBI searched for forty-five years, then put the case aside.
The money was by the river. So where did he go?
db-cooper.challenge:
🧩 You're the detective:

B) He survived and lived under a new name
C) He planted the cash to mislead everyone
Answer with a letter 👇 Best answer gets pinned 📌

beats: Five warplanes vanished. Then the plane sent to rescue them vanished too.
Florida, December 1945. A simple training flight.
Mid-flight, the leader radioed that his compasses had failed. He thought he was over the Florida Keys.
But he was wrong, and flew out over open sea until the fuel ran out.
The rescue plane? A ship saw an explosion. That model was known for leaking fuel.
No wreckage was ever found. So, Bermuda Triangle, or a broken compass?
flight-19.challenge:
🧩 Your compass is dead. It's mid-afternoon and the sky is clear.
How do you find the coast? 👇 Best answer gets pinned 📌

beats: In 1518, a woman started dancing in the street, and could not stop for days.
In Strasbourg, dozens soon joined her, dancing until they collapsed.
First clue: the city had suffered years of hunger and disease.
But leaders thought the cure was more dancing. They hired musicians, and it got worse.
Most historians say people feared a curse, and the fear spread like a disease.
So she may not have danced for joy, but from fear.
dancing-plague-1518.challenge:
🧩 Which fits best?
A) Mass panic and fear of a curse
B) Bread poisoned by a fungus
C) Something else
Answer with a letter 👇 Best answer gets pinned 📌

beats: Two men were found dead on a hill, with masks made of lead over their eyes.
Brazil, 1966. No wounds. No sign of a fight.
Beside them, a note: take the capsules, then wait for the signal.
But the bodies were found too late to test for poison.
Both were TV technicians who wanted to contact beings from space.
That night, a woman saw an orange glow over the hill. Was that the signal?
lead-masks.challenge:
🧩 The note said: take the capsules, then wait for the signal.
What was in those capsules, and what were they waiting for? 👇 Best answer gets pinned 📌

beats: Footprints in the snow led to the farmhouse. None led away.
Germany, 1922. Days later, all six people on the farm were murdered.
The farmer had said he heard footsteps in the attic. His keys had vanished.
But the killer did not flee. Smoke rose from the chimney, and someone fed the animals.
Police questioned over a hundred suspects. No one was ever charged.
The footprints never came back. So how long was the killer inside?
hinterkaifeck.challenge:
🧩 Using only these clues:

B) It was someone the family knew
C) Your own theory
Answer with a letter 👇 Best answer gets pinned 📌

beats: A boat was found with its engine running, food on the table, and no one aboard.
Australia, 2007. Why would three fishermen leave a running boat?
Their camera showed them relaxed and happy that first day.
But the life jackets were still on board. Whatever happened was sudden.
The coroner thought one fell in, and the other two jumped in to help.
That is why the engine was running. They meant to come back, but the wind pushed the boat away.

C) Something else
Answer with a letter 👇 Best answer gets pinned 📌

beats: The world's most famous female pilot flew into the Pacific, and never came back.
1937. Amelia Earhart had almost flown around the world.
Her target was Howland Island, a flat speck barely two kilometres long.
But her last message said: we must be on you, but cannot see you.
Most experts think she ran out of fuel and crashed at sea. Some think she landed on an empty island.
She may have passed within miles of Howland, and never seen it.

C) Something else
Answer with a letter 👇 Best answer gets pinned 📌

beats: A killer mailed coded letters to newspapers, mocking the police. He was never caught.
California, late 1960s. He called himself the Zodiac.
He killed at least five people, and sent four codes in his letters.
But when his hardest code was cracked in 2020, it held no name.
Two short codes are still unsolved. Before one, he wrote: My name is.
Maybe his name is hidden in that short code. Can you crack it?
